paragraphs.source_en: Other features typical for the shamanistic interpretation of the Southern African rock art, namely bleeding from the nose as a sign of trance, raised hairs, and half-man half-animal figures indicating the transformation during the trance (Lewis-Williams 1981; 2004) are virtually unknown in the Round Head art. I do not rule out that the producers of the Round Heads used altered states of consciousness. On the contrary, this important aspect of African culture certainly stretches back to prehistoric times and the presence of narcotic plants in the Uan Afuda shelter dating to the Mesolithic period (Castelletti et al. 1998) suggests this. Yet, if the trance is represented in their rock art, it does not have the same form and elements as those in South Africa.
